subject: Copywriting
title: Cultural Adaptation of Slogans
description: A quick, practical guide to Cultural Adaptation of Slogans.

hook.text: KFC's 'Finger Lickin' Good' translated to 'Eat Your Fingers Off' in Chinese. Global slogans need local adaptation.

buildup.text: Pepsi's 'Come Alive' became 'Pepsi brings your ancestors back from the dead' in China.

discovery.text: Smart brands 'transcreate' rather than translate. They keep the feeling while changing the words completely.

twist.text: Some slogans need no translation. Nike's swoosh and 'Just Do It' work globally because the emotion is universal.

climax.text: Coca-Cola adapts its slogan per market.

punchline.text: Don't translate slogans. Transcreate them. Feeling, not words.

quiz.question: What is 'transcreation'?
options: Adapting the feeling of a message for another culture
Creating a new slogan for each country

details.summary: Global brands face the challenge of translating slogans across languages and cultures without losing meaning or creating embarrassment. Pepsi's 'Come Alive with Pepsi' was reportedly translated in Chinese as 'Pepsi brings your ancestors back from the dead.' Adaptation requires cultural fluency...
details.whyItMatters: Globalization demands slogans that work across dozens of languages and cultures. Poor adaptation can cause brand damage, while skillful localization strengthens global brand coherence.
takeaways: Direct translation often fails because idioms don't cross borders
Transcreation recreates the intent and emotion in a new language
Some brands use universal slogans; others adapt for each market

faq.question: What is transcreation and how does it differ from translation?
faq.answer: Translation converts words from one language to another. Transcreation recreates the emotional intent, cultural context, and persuasive impact in the target language. A transcreated slogan may use completely different words but evoke the same feeling.

faq.question: What are famous examples of slogan translation failures?
faq.answer: KFC's 'Finger Lickin' Good' was reportedly rendered in Chinese as 'Eat your fingers off.' The HSBC bank had to rebrand entirely after 'Assume Nothing' translated as 'Do Nothing' in several markets. These failures drove the rise of transcreation as a discipline.
